statement: R^n is the standard n-dimensional space consisting of all real column vectors with n components; addition and scalar multiplication act component by component.

anchors.quote: The space $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$ consists of all column vectors v with n components.
$\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$ contains all column vectors with n real components.

statement: A real vector space is a set of vectors with rules for addition and multiplication by real numbers; the operations must produce vectors in the space and the eight conditions must hold.

anchors.quote: The addition and the multiplication must produce vectors that are in the space.
These eight conditions are required of every vector space.

statement: Z is the vector space consisting only of the zero vector; it is the smallest possible vector space and, inside R^3, the subspace containing just (0,0,0).

anchors.quote: Z The vector space that consists only of a zero vector.
The vector space Z contains exactly one vector (zero). No space can do without that zero vector.

statement: A subspace of a vector space is a set of vectors (including 0) closed under addition and scalar multiplication, so all linear combinations stay in the set.

anchors.quote: A subspace of a vector space is a set of vectors (including 0) that satisfies two requirements
Those operations leave us in the subspace.

statement: The two subspace requirements combine into one: a subspace containing v and w must contain every linear combination cv + dw.

anchors.quote: A subspace containing v and w must contain all linear combinations
In short, all linear combinations stay in the subspace.

name_en: Every subspace contains the zero vector
name_zh: 每个子空间都包含零向量
statement: Every subspace must contain the zero vector; this follows directly from the scalar-multiplication rule by choosing c = 0.

anchors.quote: First fact: Every subspace contains the zero vector.
but it follows directly from rule (ii).

statement: A line through the origin is a subspace: multiplying a vector on the line by a scalar or adding two vectors on the line keeps you on the line, but the line must pass through (0,0,0).

anchors.quote: Lines through the origin are also subspaces.
the subspace SS is the line through v.

statement: A plane through the origin in R^3 is a subspace: sums and scalar multiples of in-plane vectors stay in the plane. Planes that miss the origin are not subspaces.

anchors.quote: If we add two vectors in the plane, their sum is in the plane.
Planes that don't contain the origin fail those tests. Those planes are not subspaces.

name_zh: 矩阵 A 的列空间
statement: The column space of A consists of all linear combinations of the columns of A, i.e. all vectors Ax; it is a subspace of R^m.

anchors.quote: The column space consists of all linear combinations of the columns.
It is a vector space made up of column vectors.

statement: C(A) denotes the column space of A: the set of all linear combinations of the columns of A.

anchors.quote: The column space of A is denoted by
C(A) contains not just then columns of A, but all their combinations Ax.

name_en: Solvability of Ax=b via the column space
statement: The system Ax = b is solvable if and only if b lies in the column space of A; then b is a combination of the columns and the coefficients give a solution x.

anchors.quote: The right side b has to be in the column space produced by A on the left side, or no solution!
is solvable if and only if b is in the column space of A.
